note: Item wording is the canonical English Bedtime Procrastination Scale, transcribed verbatim from the numbered Appendix of Kroese FM, De Ridder DT, Evers C, Adriaanse MA (2014) Front Psychol 5:611, doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2014.00611 (CC BY 3.0); the trailing '(R)' scoring markers on items 2, 3, 7 and 9 were stripped from item_text and are instead encoded in option_text (see below) -- that is the only deviation from literal transcription. The study was administered in Chinese (the Zhang, Huang & You 2021 revision, Chinese J Mental Health 35(12):1049-53, a subscription Chinese-language journal). No Chinese wording exists anywhere in scope: the only deposit is S1 File (10.1371/journal.pone.0331340.s001), a single-sheet .xlsx whose 115 headers are bare codes (Q1-Q4, T0SA1..T2PE3, 'T0Average score for BPS'...) with no label layer, and the PLOS article itself prints no items. So English ships in the base fields under the 2026-09-01 fallback and the _translated columns are omitted. text_source=translated_substitute; translation_source=mixed -- item_text is the instrument publisher's own English (Kroese et al. 2014), option_text is this study's own English rendering of the administered anchors. option_text: Yu et al. (2025) Measures section states '1 = never; 2 = sometimes; 3 = sometimes; 4 = often; 5 = always' -- the duplicated label at 2 and 3 is the source's own defect and is transcribed as printed rather than silently repaired, since there is no way to tell which of the two is wrong. Those five labels are shipped in ascending order for BP1/4/5/6/8 and in DESCENDING order for BP2/BP3/BP7/BP9, because the live resp for those four items is the already-reverse-scored value, not the administered answer: the study's own 'T0Average score for BPS' column equals the plain mean of the stored T0BP1..T0BP9 columns (max |diff| 0.0044, rounding), and all 36 pairwise inter-item correlations are positive in every wave (T0 0.48-0.68) even though the paper states 'Four of the entries were reverse scoring questions' -- impossible if those four were stored raw. See verify_yu_2025_bedtime_procrastination.R. mapping_basis=paper_order: data/yu_2025_mobile_addiction_sleep.py renames source columns T{0,1,2}BP{i} -> BP{i} (a number-preserving rename, not positional), but nothing in the source file or the article ties code number i to instrument item i, so that alignment is inferred from the instrument's own 1-9 numbering and is NOT verifiable from the data (see verification row: PARTIAL). instructions left blank -- Yu et al. report none, and Kroese's appendix instruction names anchors ('(almost) never'/'(almost) always') that contradict the administered anchors shipped in option_text. Step 3b check: live data is 9 items, resp 1-5, 3 waves, 376 ids -- matches the BPS as the paper describes it. Rights: no reserved right locatable for the BPS; Kroese et al. (2014) publish the full scale in a CC BY 3.0 article with no permission, fee, non-commercial or no-derivatives clause, and the instrument carries no row in instrument_rights_register.csv.
public_note: Item text for yu_2025_bedtime_procrastination is the canonical English Bedtime Procrastination Scale (Kroese et al. 2014); the study administered a Chinese revision whose wording is published nowhere in the deposit or the article. Two caveats on the response options: the source paper's own anchor list prints 'sometimes' twice (1 = never; 2 = sometimes; 3 = sometimes; 4 = often; 5 = always) and is transcribed as printed, and for BP2, BP3, BP7 and BP9 the stored resp is the already-reverse-scored value rather than the administered answer, so those four items carry the anchors in descending order (resp 1 = always ... 5 = never)

source_ref: Yu W, Zhou X, Li B, Huang J (2025) PLOS ONE 20(9):e0331340, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0331340 (Measures section; S1 File s001.xlsx); wording from Zhang & Zhang (2022) IJERPH 19(18):11451, doi:10.3390/ijerph191811451, PMC9517028, Table 1; data/yu_2025_mobile_addiction_sleep.py
note: Instrument identified from the paper's Measures section: "The Physical Activity Rating Scale compiled by Liang Deqing was used to measure physical activity intensity, duration, and frequency. A 5-point Likert scale was used" (Yu, Zhou, Li & Huang 2025, PLOS ONE 20(9):e0331340, CC BY 4.0). The paper prints NO item wording and NO per-item statistics. Administered language is Chinese (376 high-school students in Province S, online questionnaire); the administered Chinese wording is not recoverable within scope -- the only deposit file is S1 File (s001.xlsx), whose sharedStrings table holds nothing but the 115 column codes Q1-Q4 / T{0,1,2}{SA1-22, BP1-9, PE1-3} / the nine 'Average score for ...' headers and the 5-digit participant codes, and the article carries no other supplement. So the 2026-09-01 fallback applies: English ships in the base fields, the _translated columns are omitted, language=Chinese. text_source=canonical PARS-3 wording as reproduced IN FULL (three stems plus all fifteen option cells) in Table 1, 'Questionnaire on the physical exercise of primary school students', of Zhang & Zhang (2022), IJERPH 19(18):11451, doi 10.3390/ijerph191811451, PMC9517028, CC BY 4.0 (fullTextXML sha256 53ece95cbfe7238f9e12093a51a1f5b128368f481e71e0fc3095dfcc46e5f274, fetched 2026-09-16) -- hence translation_source=third_party_english. Deviations from that source, all deliberate: the leading item numbers ('1. ', '2. ', '3. '), the source's own dimension annotations ('(Test of training intensity)', '(Test for training time)', '(Test of training frequency)') and the option letters ('A. '..'E. ') were stripped; A..E map to resp 1..5, the canonical PARS-3 raw coding and the coding stored in the deposit (all three columns run 1-5). Nothing else was reworded; en dashes in '11-20 min' etc. are the source's. Option bins cross-check against two further CC BY descriptions of the same instrument (PMC13473334, PMC12487090). mapping_basis=paper_order: data/yu_2025_mobile_addiction_sleep.py does a number-preserving rename T0PE1/T1PE1/T2PE1 -> PE1 (not positional), so the IRW code tracks the source column number exactly, but the source column names carry no text and the deposit has no label layer, so PE1=intensity / PE2=duration / PE3=frequency is inferred from the paper's stated dimension order and the canonical PARS-3 questionnaire order (intensity, duration, frequency -- Zhang & Zhang Table 1; the paper's own product-scoring description). Step 5b = NO_ROUTE and the assignment is NOT verified against data; see verify_yu_2025_physical_activity.R. Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv carries no PARS-3 row; no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is locatable for the Liang Deqing (1994, Chinese Journal of Mental Health 1:5-6) revision of Hashimoto's scale, and the wording actually copied comes from a CC BY 4.0 MDPI article that reproduces the questionnaire in full. Silence is permission, so it ships; no register row written (a round may write block rows only). Step 3b: table name matches the live data -- 3 items, resp 1-5, 3 waves, and the deposit's PE block reproduces the paper's three published PA alphas 0.828/0.688/0.730 exactly.
public_note: Item text for yu_2025_physical_activity is a third-party paper's published English rendering of the Chinese-administered PARS-3 (Zhang & Zhang 2022, IJERPH 19:11451, Table 1), not the wording the study's adolescents read, and the assignment of PE1/PE2/PE3 to intensity/duration/frequency is inferred from the paper's stated dimension order rather than verified against the data -- the source publishes no per-item statistics, and every PA-block statistic it does publish (alpha 0.828/0.688/0.730, KMO) is unchanged by any relabelling of the three items

source_ref: Yuebo Q, Halili SH, Abdul Razak R (2024) 'Online learning success model for adults in open and distance education in Western China', PLOS ONE 19(2):e0297515, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0297515 (CC BY 4.0) -- S1 Appendix 'The items with their sources' (.s002, DOCX), which prints each item against its own code in a Code column; S1 Data (.s001, CSV), whose NB1..NB16 headers are the item codes.
note: Item wording transcribed verbatim from S1 Appendix, with two disclosed deviations: the appendix's leading item numbering ('12.') was stripped, and the shared stem 'After using online learning system, I am able to perform these tasks:' -- printed inside the NB1 cell but grammatically governing the whole academic-development block -- is shipped once as section_prompt for NB1-NB5 rather than repeated in item_text. Sections follow the appendix's own three Benefits sub-headings: _1 academic development (NB1-5), _2 career development (NB6-11), _3 personal development (NB12-16); the career and personal blocks have no printed prompt, so their section_prompt is blank. option_text is blank for all 80 rows: the paper states only a '5-point Likert scale' and neither the paper, the appendix nor the S1 Data CSV prints any anchor labels, so nothing was invented and no scale point was padded with its own number. ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: the survey ran in Western China and the paper's instrumentation section describes 'a rigorous two-way translation process' used 'to ensure the accuracy of the Chinese scales in comparison to their English counterparts', so respondents read Chinese. The Chinese wording is in neither supplement -- S1 Data holds only headers and integers, S1 Appendix is English throughout (zero CJK characters) -- so the study's own English is shipped in the base fields as the fallback, language=Chinese, _translated columns omitted. MAPPING: data/yuebo_2024_online_learning.py melts the source columns keeping their names, so item IS the S1 Data header (core model pattern 1), and the appendix prints the same code beside each item; 16/16 reconcile (see verify_yuebo_2024_netbenefit.R). RIGHTS: the NB items are adapted from Hebert & Hauf (2015), Orpen (1994) and Chen & Huang (2017) -- journal-published research scales with no test publisher; no fee, no-redistribution, non-commercial or permission clause was locatable for any of them, instrument_rights_register.csv carries no row for them, and the wording IRW copied is from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS supplement. Silence is permission, so it ships.
public_note: Item text for yuebo_2024_netbenefit is the study's own English version of a questionnaire that was administered in Chinese; the administered Chinese wording is published in neither the paper nor its supplements. No response-option labels are shipped because the source states only that the items used a 5-point Likert scale and prints no anchors
